posts.text: For background on who is actually inside Delaney Hall and what the data shows about the population, I did a full profile this week: austinkocher.substack.com/p/…

The protests started over conditions inside the facility such as: medical neglect, illness and people held past approved release dates. The debate over protest tactics is real but it tends to pull focus from the people inside who have very limited ways to raise alarms.

DHS said visits were suspended because protests made it "unsafe" for families and lawyers to access the facility. However, Governor Sherrill said she didn't cave to that framing and pushed for visits to resume, which they did Sunday.

Newark Mayor Ras Baraka imposed a curfew within a half-mile of the facility after clashes between protesters and police escalated over the weekend. Three people were arrested Saturday night, including one on a weapons charge.

Protests at Delaney Hall in Newark have now been going on for more than a week. The state police have been deployed, there's a curfew and family visits to the facility were suspended. And then restored.

288

288 people inside Delaney Hall signed a letter this week describing medical neglect, illness spreading through the facility, and people held past their approved release dates with no notice to their families. This is a second letter like this in three months.

5

5 Suicides in ICE detention so far in 2026. NBC News has reviewed over 1,000 emergency calls from six facilities this as the highest yearly total in at least two decades and we're not even halfway through the year. 

nbcnews.com/politics/immigra…

$18,000

The new proposed deportation fine per person, up from $5,130. DHS has already issued $36 billion in fines to about 65,000 people, averaging $553,000 each. Officials say most of it won't be collected. Public comment period closes June 22.

57,000–58,000

That's roughly how many people are in ICE detention right now but we can't confirm it because ICE's public data is more than a month out of date. The American public currently has no official way to verify how many people the government is holding.

145,000

That's how many U.S. citizen children have had at least one parent arrested by ICE since January 2025. Brookings researchers estimated this by cross-referencing ICE arrest data with census data. The actual number could be higher. 

Link: brookings.edu/articles/the-a…
Five numbers from last week's immigration enforcement. Each one tells a story the news cycle didn't slow down enough to explain.

Full write up below. I hope the data in the report is useful to reporters, researchers, policymakers, elected leaders, and the broad public. Feel free to use any of these tables and graphs with attribution. 

austinkocher.substack.com/p/…
And where were most people in DH originally arrested? Mostly in NJ and NY, although some were transferred from outside the region.

Can ICE deport people in DH? Mostly no. As of mid-March, the majority of people held at Delaney Hall—84.2%—did not have a final removal order. In the past, the gov often chose not to waste taxpayer $$$ detaining people it can't deport and don't represent a threat to pub safety.

What about all 10,311 people to pass through DH since May 2025? Just two (0.02%) had homicide conviction (0.07% if you incl all manslaughter), 24 (0.2%) sex. assault conviction, 19 (0.2%) drug traffic, 9 (0.09%) robbery, 12 (0.1%) agg assault.

Is DH holding "murderers, rapists, pedophiles and drug traffickers"? ICE's data says vast majority have no conviction (88.3%) + large majority have no crim history (70.5%). If you were looking for an ICE facility that holds a large number of dangerous criminals, DH isn't it.

In a PR on May 25, ICE pushed back on criticisms of DH: “These sanctuary politicians should be thanking ICE for removing murderers, rapists, pedophiles, and drug traffickers from their communities. We need politicians cooperate with us to get criminals out of their state.”
"In at least four states, migrants detained in ICE facilities have launched hunger strikes in recent weeks to protest the conditions in which they are being held."

I'm looking for another org or two that could speak to local efforts to cut ties with an FBI Joint Terrorism Task Force. A handful of cities have done it, including Portland and Oakland. I want to know who's next! 👀 

This is for reporting @truthout.org. RTs appreciated #journorequest
